title: The Capacitor Bench
summary: Charge a capacitor, design a parallel plate and slide in a dielectric with the battery connected or not.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can use C = Q/V, find the capacitance of parallel plates, and say how a dielectric changes C, V, Q and the field with the battery connected or disconnected.

levels.title: Charge a capacitor
levels.adds: Baseline: C = Q/V, so the charge on the plates is Q = CV, with one plate +Q and the other −Q (Ex 2.8).
hints: Q = CV. With C in pF and V in volts, Q comes out in pC; divide by 1000 for nC.
To find the voltage instead, use V = Q/C.
One plate carries +Q and the other −Q.

levels.title: The parallel plate
levels.adds: New idea: C = ε₀A/d, so halving the gap doubles C, and a dielectric multiplies C by K (Ex 2.5, 2.8).
hints: C = ε₀A/d, with A in m² and d in metres. Rearrange for d.
C is inversely proportional to the gap: half the gap, twice the capacitance.
A dielectric of constant K multiplies the capacitance by K.

levels.title: Slide in a dielectric
levels.adds: New idea: with the battery connected V stays fixed and Q rises by K; disconnected, Q stays fixed and V falls by K (Ex 2.9, Example 2.8).
hints: The dielectric multiplies the capacitance by K in both cases.
Battery connected: V is fixed, so Q = CV grows by the factor K.
Disconnected: Q cannot change, so V = Q/C falls by the factor K.

misconceptions: The capacitance depends on the charge on the plates
Halving the gap halves the capacitance
A dielectric changes the charge whether or not the battery is connected
The potential difference rises when a dielectric is inserted
